title: The AI Ledger
introduction: The October 26–November 1 edition, with separately dated supplements reviewed through November 9. Today: the official Fable 5.2/Mythos 5.2 launch and Claude Code 2.1.321. The November 8 forecast is resolved against its original criterion, with a new November 10–15 follow-up. Earlier editions and supplements remain archived. Source dates are announcement dates, not crawl dates; confidence is qualitative, not a probability.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 9: Fable 5.2 launches; Mythos access stays gated
items.summary: Anthropic released Fable 5.2 across its platforms. Mythos 5.2 shares the underlying model but is restricted to verified cyber and life-sciences organizations. Fable has stronger safeguards.
items.whyItMatters: Standard input/output pricing is $8/$40 per million tokens; optional fast mode costs $16/$80. Compare total task costs, not token rates alone.
items.confidenceReason: The announcement verifies availability and pricing. Claimed capability and speed gains are vendor results, not independent replication.
items.historicalContext: This November 9 launch follows 5.1. It is separate from earlier user-intent reporting; similar testimonials do not establish that report’s identity.

sources.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
sources.authenticityReason: Official announcement explicitly dated November 9; verified through indexed first-party content. Performance claims are vendor-reported.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 9: Claude Code adds Fable 5.2 and security fixes
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.321 makes Fable 5.2 the default Fable model. Release notes report fixes for MCP OAuth secrets following cross-host redirects and several Bash permission and sandbox checks.
items.whyItMatters: Review this upgrade for agent environments using MCP credentials or shell tools. Remote Control also gains a settings-file option that stops new sessions if the file changes until restart.
items.confidenceReason: The stable release is official. Security fixes remain publisher claims, not proof of complete protection.
items.historicalContext: Released November 9 at 19:22 UTC, following 2.1.319 on November 6. This satisfies the documented-control-update forecast published November 8.

sources.title: Claude Code v2.1.321 release
sources.authenticityReason: Official repository release dated November 9, 19:22 UTC; marked latest rather than prerelease. Fixes are publisher-reported, not independently audited.

items.title: Added Nov 8 · Nov 6 release: OpenCode improves scripted sessions
items.summary: OpenCode 2.2.6 adds opt-in MCP connection pooling across projects and worktree creation for scripted runs. Its run command now waits for background jobs before exiting.
items.whyItMatters: CI jobs need explicit timeouts: a server or watcher that never exits can keep the run open indefinitely. Pooling may reduce duplicate MCP processes; worktrees separate concurrent edits.
items.confidenceReason: The official release documents these features and their limits. No performance measurements or independent security audit were performed for this issue.
items.historicalContext: Published November 6 at 23:37 UTC. This is a catch-up, not a November 8 release; it extends the worktree and compaction controls covered in 2.2.5.

sources.title: OpenCode v2.2.6 release
sources.authenticityReason: Official publisher repository release; GitHub API publication timestamp verified November 8. Release notes establish announced behavior, not independent reliability testing.

items.title: Added Nov 8 · Nov 6 release: Copilot CLI adds session controls
items.summary: Copilot CLI 1.0.107 adds opt-in local session-management tools, a command to open the current session in VS Code, and a setting to sandbox extension processes.
items.whyItMatters: The notes also report that Autopilot no longer implements recommendations after review-only requests. Teams should test that boundary rather than assume the fix eliminates all unintended edits.
items.confidenceReason: GitHub's official release supplies the changes and date; the behavior fix is publisher-reported and has not been independently tested here.
items.historicalContext: Published November 6 at 20:37 UTC. This builds on Copilot's cross-surface workflow and is separate from the previously covered JetBrains Air availability.

sources.title: GitHub v1.0.107 release
sources.authenticityReason: Official publisher repository release; GitHub API publication timestamp verified November 8. Release notes establish announced behavior, not independent reliability testing.

items.title: Added Nov 7 · Nov 6 release: Claude Code backgrounds MCP tasks
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.319 adds background execution for MCP tasks and a permission setting that denies calls instead of waiting for a prompt. Finished subagents can also be reopened from the task list.
items.whyItMatters: Unattended workflows gain clearer control over permission waits and long-running tools. The release also reports permission-bypass and sandbox-escape fixes, making upgrade review worthwhile.
items.confidenceReason: Anthropic’s official release notes establish the announced changes. The fixes are vendor-reported, not an independent security audit or a guarantee that all bypasses are closed.
items.historicalContext: Published November 6 at 17:04 UTC, before the previous supplement’s timestamp but omitted from that edition. This is a catch-up addition, not a November 7 release. It follows 2.1.318’s per-fork effort controls.

sources.title: Claude Code v2.1.319 release
sources.authenticityReason: Official anthropics repository release, checked November 7. GitHub’s API gives published_at as 2026-11-06T17:04:01Z; features are attributed to the publisher.

items.title: Added Nov 7 · Nov 5 launch: Inkling 2 Small arrives on Tinker
items.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Small for fine-tuning and inference on Tinker. The text-and-image model has 594 billion total parameters with 17 billion active, and supports variable reasoning effort.
items.whyItMatters: It adds a customizable option for coding agents and tool-using applications. Hosted access is available, but the launch announcement describes full Apache 2.0 weights as a future step after external safety testing and red-teaming.
items.confidenceReason: The official announcement and model card both date the release November 5. This verifies announced availability, not independent performance or completion of the promised weight release.
items.historicalContext: The second Inkling generation follows earlier checkpoints tested in OpenCode as Fledge-Alpha. This November 7 catch-up preserves the original launch date rather than treating later coverage as a new release.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 6: Codex CLI 0.167 improves session navigation
items.summary: OpenAI’s 0.167.0 release adds unread-result markers, backend switching that preserves drafts, and inline patch inspection while an approval prompt is open.
items.whyItMatters: These controls help developers track parallel work and inspect changes at the approval boundary.
items.confidenceReason: The official changelog dates these features November 6. It also lists compaction and provider-switching fixes; release notes are not a safety certification.
items.historicalContext: The October 27 release expanded session control; this update continues that workflow trend rather than announcing a new model.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 6: Cursor adds two-way voice conversations
items.summary: Cursor announced Grok Voice-powered calls across its Agents Window, IDE, web and iOS app. A voice agent can hand coding work to the chat agent while the conversation continues.
items.whyItMatters: Developers can ask for progress and discuss changes without waiting for a coding run to finish.
items.confidenceReason: The dated first-party announcement supports feature availability. Voice interaction does not itself demonstrate better code quality or safer execution.
items.historicalContext: This is distinct from earlier dictation, which only transcribed speech into the input box.

sources.title: Voice Chat with Agents
sources.authenticityReason: Dated release notes on the publisher’s official site or repository, checked November 6, 2026. This establishes the announced features, not independently tested reliability.

items.title: Added Nov 6 · Nov 5 announcement: Cursor deploys live apps
items.summary: Cursor can scaffold an app, provision a Postgres database and authentication, and publish a hosted link. The feature is available on paid plans with cloud agents enabled.
items.whyItMatters: The workflow extends coding into deployment. Publishing requires an explicit action and passing security checks; administrators can override blocked publishes.
items.confidenceReason: Official release notes establish the feature and gating. Automated checks should not be treated as proof that an app is secure; access and secrets still need review.
items.historicalContext: The announcement moves beyond localhost workflows. GitHub and Cursor Origin repositories are supported; GitLab support is described as forthcoming.

sources.title: Build Live Apps in Cursor

items.title: Added Nov 6 · Nov 5 release: Hermes unifies sessions and adds tool budgets
items.summary: Nous Research’s Hermes Agent 0.23 puts session ownership in one gateway, adds a browser workspace and conversation rewind, and introduces spend-limit approvals for paid MCP tools.
items.whyItMatters: Cross-surface continuity and tool budgets are useful harness controls. Upgrade carefully: legacy browser tools are removed and MCP-server launch commands change.
items.confidenceReason: The official repository explicitly dates the release November 5. Its behavior and performance claims have not been independently tested for this newsletter.
items.historicalContext: The release consolidates the 0.22 patch series. Browser workspace access is off by default and must be enabled explicitly.

sources.authenticityReason: Dated release notes on the publisher’s official site or repository, checked November 6, 2026. This establishes the announced features, not independently tested reliability.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 5: GPT-6 Cyber launches with restricted access
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber for security research, initially through the API and Codex for selected approved Daybreak Red customers. Its system card identifies it as a cybersecurity-specialized variant of GPT-6 Astra.
items.whyItMatters: Access remains gated. OpenAI rates its cybersecurity capability Critical under its Preparedness Framework; teams should distinguish that capability classification from a guarantee of safe operation.
items.confidenceReason: The dated announcement and system card establish the release and restrictions. Results are vendor evaluations: the card reports mixed alignment performance against Astra, including weaker results on stopping after warnings and final-answer disclosure of blockers.
items.historicalContext: It follows GPT-5.6 Cyber, which OpenAI rated High for cybersecurity. Wider GPT-6 Cyber access is planned, without a firm date in the announcement.

sources.title: GPT-6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
sources.authenticityReason: Official company announcement explicitly dated November 5, checked that day. It separates initial availability from planned access expansion.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 5: PLaMo 3 Translate releases downloadable weights
items.summary: Preferred Networks announced PLaMo 3 Translate weights in four sizes, from 0.8B to 31B parameters, supporting 53 languages. The models are intended for translation on local devices and private servers.
items.whyItMatters: Local deployment offers another option for translation workloads. Free commercial use requires registration and the PLaMo Community License’s ¥1 billion-or-less revenue/sales condition for the user or affiliates in the most recent fiscal year; commercial use above that threshold needs a separate license.
items.confidenceReason: PFN’s dated announcement supports the release and license summary. Translation-quality comparisons remain vendor-reported; local performance depends on model size and hardware.
items.historicalContext: PFN updated its hosted translation service to the third-generation model on October 7. November 5 is the weight-release milestone, rather than the first appearance of the model family.

sources.title: PFN releases PLaMo 3 Translate open-weight models
sources.authenticityReason: Original Japanese company announcement dated November 5. Its correction clarifies that the revenue threshold includes ¥1 billion.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 5: METR reports faster AI R&D at Anthropic, with major caveats
items.summary: After an August–October assessment with access to internal data, METR estimates that Anthropic’s progress on well-specified tasks is roughly twice its March 2024–October 2025 pace. METR believes AI-assisted R&D likely accounts for most of the current acceleration, with substantial uncertainty.
items.whyItMatters: This adds evidence about models helping build subsequent models. METR says Anthropic redacted most of the evidence it found most informative, limiting public scrutiny of its conclusions.
items.confidenceReason: The report is primary research from the evaluator. Attribution to AI is an uncertain assessment, not a controlled causal result; benchmark scope, other drivers and redactions limit generalization.
items.historicalContext: Published November 5 about an assessment ending October 29. It concerns development progress on defined tasks, not a newly released model or proof of fully autonomous AI research.

sources.title: Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026
sources.authenticityReason: Original dated assessment on METR’s site. External authorship is distinct from independent reproducibility: access and publication redactions depended on Anthropic.

items.title: Added Nov 5 · Nov 4 announcement: Images 2.6 expands creation and editing
items.summary: OpenAI announced Images 2.6 for ChatGPT, Codex and the API on November 4. API options include Flare and Sunburst, with image markup, SVG exports and a complexity control; the release also adds GIF creation.
items.whyItMatters: Developers gain more control over visual assets and editing workflows. OpenAI’s faster-generation claim is vendor-reported, and actual latency depends on settings and workload.
items.confidenceReason: The official announcement confirms availability and features. It does not provide an independently reproduced speed comparison.
items.historicalContext: This is a November 4 release added during the November 5 review. The source gives no publication time, so this edition makes no claim that it appeared after the previous daily cutoff.

sources.title: Introducing Images 2.6
sources.authenticityReason: Official product announcement explicitly dated November 4. The source date is preserved rather than using the date of later news coverage.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: VS Code previews mixed-harness sessions
items.summary: VS Code 1.145 adds a preview that groups Copilot, Claude and Codex chats within one session, with separate model, agent and permission settings. The stable release also adds cron schedules and workspace custom agents for local automations.
items.whyItMatters: Developers can compare agents without splitting related conversations across separate sessions. Mixed-harness sessions require the preview setting; cron schedules do not apply to cloud automations.
items.confidenceReason: Microsoft's official release notes establish the features and their preview limits. No independent productivity improvement is claimed.
items.historicalContext: Previously, nested sessions inherited their parent's harness. This changes session organization rather than introducing a new underlying model.

sources.title: Visual Studio Code 1.145 release notes
sources.authenticityReason: Official notes explicitly date the stable release November 4, 2026 and mark mixed-harness nested sessions as Preview.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: Claude Code adds per-fork effort controls
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.318 lets a mod's model fork choose its own reasoning effort, independently of the session. It also exposes stored sign-in expiry in command-line status and JSON output, with advance warnings for unattended text runs.
items.whyItMatters: Small delegated jobs can use lower effort without changing the main session. Expiry visibility gives developers a clearer signal before unattended jobs lose authentication.
items.confidenceReason: Anthropic's official release notes confirm the changes; their effect on cost and reliability was not independently measured.
items.historicalContext: This adds control at the individual mod-fork level. The same release fixes conversation continuation and idle-compaction failures.

sources.title: Claude Code v2.1.318 release

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: Tencent announces Hy4, with weights still to come
items.summary: Tencent's November 4 announcement describes Hy4's visual understanding and computer-use capabilities, and availability across its products. Vercel had already announced Hy4 access through AI Gateway on November 3, including image input and a one-million-token context window.
items.whyItMatters: API availability and downloadable weights are different milestones. Tencent says model weights and system cards will arrive in the coming days; the announcement does not establish that they are available now.
items.confidenceReason: A Tencent-issued announcement and Vercel's own integration changelog support the availability claims. Performance descriptions remain vendor-reported.
items.historicalContext: Hy4 follows Hy4 Preview. November 3 gateway access and November 4 corporate announcement are distinct dates, not two separate model launches.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: OpenAI announces plans to acquire Pierre
items.summary: OpenAI says it will acquire Pierre, the developer-tools company behind Code Storage. Closing remains subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals; the companies remain independent until then.
items.whyItMatters: The planned acquisition could bring source-control and code-review tools more closely into Codex. It is not a completed transaction or an announcement that new integrations are available today.
items.confidenceReason: The official announcement establishes the stated plan and closing conditions, not a guaranteed closing date or delivered product roadmap.
items.historicalContext: Pierre’s Trees and Diffs libraries already support file browsing and code review in the Codex app. The announcement builds on that existing relationship.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 3: Claude Code adds fail-closed hook controls
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.317 adds an Agent SDK hook option that blocks an action if its callback fails, warnings about unexpected connectors on scheduled cloud tasks, and checks before web or shell calls transmit the account email address.
items.whyItMatters: These controls affect how coding agents handle failures and external actions. The release also adds a gateway-admin cost report, with spend grouped by date, developer or identity-provider group.
items.confidenceReason: Official release notes establish the announced changes. They do not independently prove that every failure or unintended transmission is prevented.
items.historicalContext: The October 31 release added subagent-effort and pooled-budget controls. November 3 extends operational oversight with hook-failure handling and cost reporting.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 3: Copilot arrives in JetBrains Air
items.summary: GitHub announced Copilot integration in JetBrains Air through Agent Client Protocol. Developers can track parallel sessions and review changes in context, using their Copilot subscription for local or cloud coding tasks.
items.whyItMatters: Cloud use requires an Air Teams-enabled business organization and administrator enablement. Tasks use Copilot rather than JetBrains AI credits; Air analytics do not show Copilot usage, and Air cannot set its spending limits.
items.confidenceReason: GitHub's dated first-party announcement describes availability and limitations. Access still depends on account, subscription and administrator settings.
items.historicalContext: After GitHub's October 28 connected-cloud rollout, this adds a JetBrains Air entry point. The new integration is distinct from the existing Copilot plugin.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 2: LongCat-2.5 reaches the API
items.summary: LongCat's official API changelog marks LongCat-2.5 available on November 2, following a November 1 announcement. The company positions it for visual understanding and long-running coding tasks, and lists compatibility with Claude Code, Codex and Hermes.
items.whyItMatters: A new model can enter existing coding workflows without a wholly new harness. Compatibility is the vendor's claim, not evidence that every setup works unchanged or that it outperforms alternatives.
items.confidenceReason: Official dated API documentation establishes the availability announcement. Capability and harness-compatibility claims remain vendor-reported and were not independently tested here.
items.historicalContext: The same changelog dates LongCat-2.5-Preview to September 25. The full-model blog is dated November 1; the API availability entry is November 2. This is a preview-to-release progression, not two separate model launches.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra rolls out
items.summary: OpenAI announced Terra for its API, ChatGPT Work and Codex—not Chat. Listed standard API prices are $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
items.whyItMatters: Teams have another deployment option; they should test quality on their own workloads instead of treating price as a capability ranking.
items.confidenceReason: Official release documentation establishes the announcement and listed terms, not independent comparative performance.
items.historicalContext: GPT-4o mini's July 2024 launch also emphasized cost-efficient deployment. Different capability classes make raw token-price comparisons misleading.

items.summary: The October 30 release adds percentage-based context buffers, worktree/base-branch shortcuts, and fixes for context-window errors and model-switch reasoning handling.
items.whyItMatters: A buffer expressed as a percentage can adapt across model context sizes. These are concrete harness ergonomics and reliability changes, not a new underlying model.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: Previously the buffer setting accepted a token count; percentage support makes one configuration more portable across differently sized model windows.

items.title: Resolved Nov 9 · November 9–15 harness-control forecast: met
items.summary: We expect at least one stable Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI or OpenCode release to add or fix a documented permission, background-task or session-control behavior.
items.whyItMatters: These controls affect unattended reliability even without a new frontier model.
items.confidenceReason: Several independent harnesses shipped such changes this week. This is an editorial extrapolation from recent releases, not a vendor promise or a numerical probability. Resolution November 9: Claude Code 2.1.321 documents permission and session-control fixes in a stable release, meeting the original criterion. The original forecast is preserved in the November 8 archive.
items.historicalContext: The November 2–8 control-upgrade forecast was met by the November 3 Claude Code hook controls and later releases. That original forecast remains unchanged in the archived November 7 snapshot.
